claims.paraphrase: Page title.
Intro listing the topics with pointers to the image and publish pages.
Section heading.
The sidebar names each concept and selecting one lists its entries with a status per row.
New opens a create dialog for title, address, and sometimes date, then lands in the editor.
The address becomes part of the published location through the permalink pattern.
A blank address fills from the title as it is typed.
The generated address is lowercase with hyphens for spaces and punctuation.
The address can be typed instead of generated.
The address can be changed later from Details.
Section heading.
The title has its own large field above the editor.
A toolbar with Write and Preview tabs sits above the text.
Preview shows the entry roughly as the site will render it.
Every entry opens on Write.
The body is markdown and the toolbar buttons insert the marks.
A rich paste converts headings, emphasis, links, and lists and reduces other elements to plain text.
Preview has a device-width control remembered per device.
A Details panel opens from a header icon.
Details holds tags, date, and lead picture where declared.
Hidden is a Details-panel checkbox.
The entry address is changed in Details.
Characterizes Details as settings configured once.
Section heading.
The toolbar groups its buttons into clusters.
The Format cluster holds Bold, Italic, Strikethrough, and Inline code.
Bold is Ctrl+B, Italic Ctrl+I, Inline code Ctrl+E, and Strikethrough has none.
The Structure cluster holds Heading, Smaller heading, both lists, Quote, and Table.
Shortcuts for Heading, Smaller heading, both list types, and Quote.
The overflow menu next to Structure carries three rarer block tools.
The Insert cluster holds link, page link, image, and where enabled fragment and block tools.
Section heading.
Web link and Link to page are separate tools.
Web link is Ctrl+K and links to an ordinary web address.
A selection becomes the link text; otherwise the dialog takes an address and words.
Link to page searches site entries and inserts a link.
Advice to use Link to page for internal targets.
An internal link survives a change of the target address.
The internal link is stored with a cairn: prefix and resolved to a real address at publish.
Section heading.
Insert image, drag, and paste start the same flow.
Pointer to the upload panel page.
The lead picture is edited in the Details panel, not the body.
Pointer to the lead picture section.
Advice on writing alt text and when to mark an image decorative.
An image lacking both stays marked as missing alt text until described.
A decorative body image stays flagged because markdown alt has no slot for the choice.
The flag does not affect publishing and the published image is still treated as decorative.
Only the lead picture stores the decorative choice and clears the flag.
An image in the draft can take a caption and placement.
The figure button wraps the image at the cursor, is dim until the cursor is on an image, then reads Edit the figure.
Defines a caption as visible text and alt text as screen-reader text.
Placements Measure, Center, Wide, and Full and how each sits relative to the text column.
A decorative image with a caption triggers a warning because a screen reader skips it.
Section heading.
Fragments are written once, published, and included through the Include a fragment control where the site has them.
An included fragment renders its current published version everywhere it is included.
A fragment inserts as an ::include line that Preview and the site resolve to the real text.
The picker says so when no fragment is published.
Section heading.
Layout blocks are colon-fenced directives whose fence lines mark the block boundaries.
Insert block opens a palette and a guided form when the site registers components.
The pencil beside Insert block reopens the form for the block at the caret.
The pencil is unavailable when the block cannot be edited as a form.
Blocks open folded and spring open when touched.
Section heading.
Introduces two in-editor reference sheets.
The question-mark button opens a one-screen syntax-to-result table.
The shortcuts sheet opens with Ctrl+/.
The sheet enumerates all chords, from Save and Publish through formatting and issue navigation.
Typed markdown always works and buttons are conveniences.
Section heading.
Display controls sit in the editor footer and change appearance only.
Focus mode dims all but the cursor paragraph.
Typewriter mode keeps the caret line roughly centered vertically while typing.
Zen hides the toolbar and controls and Escape or the shortcut restores them.
Prose and Wide switch the writing surface width.
Claims the wide surface suits tables and long addresses.
Below the small breakpoint the controls move into More formatting.
The modes are per-browser preferences and not saved to the entry.
Section heading.
Spellcheck underlines unknown words, offers suggestions and a shared-dictionary add, and can be turned off.
The underline also flags doubled words, double spaces, and repeated punctuation, never style.
A Tidy button appears only when the site has a copy-edit tool.
Tidy reads the selection when one exists, else the whole draft.
Tidy suggests fixes for spelling, grammar, and mild rewording.
Nothing changes until review, and each change shows what it removes and adds.
Judgment changes are marked Review this.
Accept fixes takes only objective fixes and never sweeps Review this changes.
Reject all rejects every proposed change.
Apply writes to the editor as one undoable step and the next save keeps it.
Typing is blocked during a Tidy review as it is on Preview.
Finishing the review restores typing.
Selecting Reject all brings typing back.
An overlong draft cannot be tidied in one pass; the error page explains the workaround.
Section heading.
Pointer to the publish page.
Save keeps changes private while working.
Publish makes changes live.
Horizontal rule.
A freshness stamp naming a review date.
